entries.appliesTo: State Board of Elections and State Administrator of Elections responding to election misinformation and disinformation

dutySources.takedown-process: § 2-110(b)(1) — 'The State Board shall maintain a portal on the State Board's website that the public may use to report election misinformation and election disinformation.'

exposure.enforcer: state-board-of-elections (civil action for damages, court costs, attorney's fees)

sources.program: § 2-110(c)(1)(i)1 — 'SHALL COMMUNICATE, DISSEMINATE, OR DISTRIBUTE TO THE PUBLIC ACCURATE INFORMATION TO CORRECT THE ELECTION MISINFORMATION OR ELECTION DISINFORMATION'
sources.enforcer: § 2-110(c)(3)(i) — 'THE STATE BOARD MAY SEEK DAMAGES, COURT COSTS, AND ATTORNEY'S FEES IN A CIVIL ACTION FILED UNDER PARAGRAPH (2)(II) OF THIS SUBSECTION'

flags: § 2-110(b) portal and periodic-review duties are preexisting law reenacted without amendment (lowercase text); the new matter in this Act is subsection (c) (uppercase)
Corrective-information mandate on the State Administrator fits no listed public-sector duty key; coded only as the free-text `program` param

State Administrator 'MAY SEEK AN INJUNCTION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE MARYLAND RULES FOR THE REMOVAL OF THE ELECTION MISINFORMATION OR ELECTION DISINFORMATION FROM ANY ONLINE PLATFORM' and may issue subpoenas under the federal Stored Communications Act (§ 2-110(c)(1)(i)2-3) — discretionary powers, no matching duty/param key
Injunctions barred against an 'INTERACTIVE COMPUTER SERVICE, AS DEFINED IN 47 U.S.C. § 230, FOR CONTENT DISSEMINATED BY ANOTHER PERSON' (§ 2-110(c)(1)(ii))

Civil-action exposure runs against private persons, campaigns, political action committees, or other legal entities — not the bound agency; damages are uncapped (no penaltyMax stated) and require 'A SHOWING BY CLEAR AND CONVINCING EVIDENCE' (§ 2-110(c)(4)) plus that the Board 'INCURS COSTS TO COMMUNICATE, DISSEMINATE, OR DISTRIBUTE TO THE PUBLIC ACCURATE INFORMATION' (§ 2-110(c)(2)(ii)2)

Civil action barred against persons exempt from § 16-905 and against a person 'WHO SEEKS TO DETECT, REPORT, PREVENT, INVESTIGATE, RESPOND TO, OR PROSECUTE PERSONS RESPONSIBLE FOR SECURITY BREACHES, IDENTITY THEFT, FRAUD, HARASSMENT, OR OTHER MALICIOUS OR ILLEGAL ACTIVITY' (§ 2-110(c)(2)(i))
Liability standard is fault-tiered: election disinformation, or 'WITH RECKLESS DISREGARD' election misinformation (§ 2-110(c)(2)(ii)1, (c)(4))

entries.appliesTo: any person who knowingly or with reckless disregard creates, uses, or disseminates an election-related deepfake

sources.prohibition: § 16-905(c) — 'A PERSON MAY NOT KNOWINGLY OR WITH RECKLESS DISREGARD CREATE, USE, OR DISSEMINATE A DEEPFAKE TO PRODUCE MATERIALLY FALSE INFORMATION'
sources.coveredSubjects: § 16-905(a)(2) — 'A REALISTIC BUT FALSE DEPICTION OF A PERSON THAT AN ORDINARY PERSON WOULD CONCLUDE IS AN ACTUAL VISUAL OR AUDIO REPRESENTATION OF THE PERSON DEPICTED'
sources.penaltyMax: § 16-905(d) — 'IS GUILTY OF A MISDEMEANOR AND ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO A FINE OF NOT MORE THAN $5,000'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 16-905(d) — 'ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO A FINE OF NOT MORE THAN $5,000 OR IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT MORE THAN 5 YEARS OR BOTH'

flags: Misdemeanor; imprisonment for not more than 5 years, or both fine and imprisonment (§ 16-905(d)) — per rule 11 only the fine is coded as penaltyMax

Two-part scienter: requires intent to impede/influence voting, misrepresent election facts, induce petition signing, or influence a vote for/against a candidate or ballot issue (§ 16-905(c)(1)), AND that the deepfake 'RESULTS, OR HAS THE INTENT TO RESULT, IN HARM TO A VOTER, POTENTIAL VOTER, OR PETITION' (§ 16-905(c)(2))

Exemptions (§ 16-905(b)): satire or parody; broadcasters airing federally required candidate ads, bona fide news with an audible/readable deceptive-media disclosure, or paid broadcasts after a good-faith vetting effort; news websites/periodicals that clearly state the media 'DOES NOT ACCURATELY REPRESENT THE SPEECH OR CONDUCT OF THE CANDIDATE'; and 'ANY ONLINE PUBLISHER OR SERVICE PROVIDER FOR ACTS THAT WOULD BE SUBJECT TO IMMUNITY UNDER 47 U.S.C. § 230'
'Deepfake' definition covers media created 'WITH THE USE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE OR OTHER DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY' (§ 16-905(a)(2)) — broader than AI-only
No election time window on the prohibition (electionWindowDays not set); enforcer of the criminal offense not named in this text
Coded ai-crimes per rule 10: this is a conduct prohibition on deceptive deepfakes, not a disclosure regime
